subject: Clarifying how overlapping context windows are billed for hybrid pilot
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acmehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: AcmeHealth Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, James Liu <james@finpay.io>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot billing question: mixed short prompts + occasional long-history calls

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited. Before we finalize the PO we need a clear example of how you will bill our hybrid workload during the 60‑day pilot. Our usage profile is: ~70% short requests (~20–50 tokens each, high QPS, batched), 25% medium multi-turn chats (up to 2k tokens context), and ~5% long analysis calls (~25–40k context) for retrospectives.

Primary asks:
- How do you account for overlapping prefixes when a short request arrives that reuses a warm KV prefix from a recent long call?
- Do you round short, batched calls up to a minimum quantum per request or per batch?
- If we hit the committed tier discount during the pilot, how are credits applied against mixed-length calls? Example invoice lines would be helpful.

We want to avoid surprises on month‑end. Can you share a worked sample for a single day with a mix of those calls?

Attachment: acme_pilot_requirements.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of ML Platforms
AcmeHealth
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, AcmeHealth Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot billing question: mixed short prompts + occasional long-history calls

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear breakdown (and for the pilot interest). Short answer: charges are per billable unit we call a "compute unit" (derived from tokenized input+output and context amortization rules), with smoothing rules that try to avoid double-charging for immediate KV reuse. That said, the best way to make this concrete is a short worked example — I’ll draft one below and loop in Ben for the invoice math and Markus for how discounts/commits apply.

High-level notes:
- Prefix/KV reuse: if a short request hits within the same active context window (default 10 minutes for pilot), we amortize the shared prefix tokens and only bill the delta tokens (plus a tiny per-request minimal quantum).
- Minimal quantum: we round per-request up to our micro-quantum of 8 tokens for streaming-short calls OR to the batch‑level quantum if we see batching at the API layer. That prevents very small spikes from generating fractional noise on invoices.
- Long calls: billed at actual token usage; long‑call cost can be smoothed across the following N minutes (we've used 30 minutes during pilots) to credit subsequent short calls that benefit from warmed state.

Below is a worked sample (cleaned) for a day with 10,000 short calls, 1,500 medium chats, and 60 long retrospectives. Ben, can you validate the numbers and produce an invoice sample? Markus — can you confirm which committed discount tier applies at the volumes in DEAL-ACME-4891?

-- Worked sample (high level):
- Short calls: 10,000 calls * (actual avg tokens 35 -> rounded to quantum 40) => billable tokens = 400k
- Medium chats: 1,500 chats * 2k tokens avg => billable tokens = 3,000k
- Long retrospectives: 60 calls * 30k tokens => billable tokens = 1,800k
- KV amortization credit applied to short calls: assume warm prefix amortization yields 10% reduction on the short calls => credit ~40k tokens
- Net billable tokens: 400k + 3,000k + 1,800k - 40k = 5,160k tokens

Attachment: none in this message (referenced Elena's sheet).

Thanks,
Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, AcmeHealth Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 12:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot billing question: mixed short prompts + occasional long-history calls

Thanks Steph — validated the worked sample and sketched a sample invoice format below. I kept everything rounded to whole tokens and added the micro-quantum rules.

Assumptions used in numbers: token price $0.0006 per token (pilot rate), micro-quantum rounding to 8 tokens per request when batching not detected, batch-level quantum when batching >1 request in a single HTTP call. KV amortization credit windows: 30 minutes for long-call carryover, 10 minutes for short-prefix reuse.

Detailed math (line items):
1) Short calls (pre-credit): 10,000 calls * max(avg_actual 35, quantum 8) = billable tokens 400,000 (we used Steph's 40 per call rounding for visibility).
2) Medium chats: 1,500 * 2,000 = 3,000,000 tokens
3) Long retrospectives: 60 * 30,000 = 1,800,000 tokens
4) KV amortization credit: -40,000 tokens (applied as a credit line)

Net tokens billed = 5,160,000 tokens
Gross charge = 5,160,000 * $0.0006 = $3,096.00
Commit discount (example): 10% commit credit applied after gross = -$309.60
Pilot invoice subtotal = $2,786.40
Tax/other fees not included.

Sample invoice lines (human readable):
- Line 1: "Short calls — micro-quantum rounding (10k calls)" — 400,000 tokens — $240.00
- Line 2: "Medium multi-turn chats" — 3,000,000 tokens — $1,800.00
- Line 3: "Long-analysis calls" — 1,800,000 tokens — $1,080.00
- Line 4: "KV amortization credit" — -40,000 tokens — -$24.00
- Line 5: "Commit discount (10%)" — -$309.60
- Total due — $2,786.40

Notes / caveats:
- If AcmeHealth enables batching on the client side (sending multiple user prompts in one request), the batch-level quantum will likely reduce short‑call billables further; we can add a line showing before/after batching.
- We can also configure a pilot-specific amortization window (e.g., extend long-call credit to 60 minutes) and show impact on pilot invoice as part of the MSA.

I attached a quick PDF sample invoice that mirrors these lines. Happy to walk through these with finance.

Attachment: acme_pilot_sample_invoice_v1.pdf

Ben Carter
Senior Billing Analyst
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot billing question: mixed short prompts + occasional long-history calls

Elena / team — quick pricing confirmation. For DEAL-ACME-4891 the committed tier that triggers at your expected monthly run‑rate (projected from the pilot numbers multiplied by seasonality) is 10% standard commit credit with the following behavior:
- Commit credits are applied against invoice subtotal after token charges and before taxes.
- Credits are proportional to monthly actuals vs committed threshold; we prorate for the pilot month if you sign mid-month.
- We will not reclassify long calls as a separate SKU during the pilot; they remain token-charged but we can ship a 'long-call smoothing' concession (one-time) that gives an additional 5% reduction on long-call tokens for the first 90 days to help with adoption.

Operational suggestion: enable client batching and set a short KV TTL on the SDK (default 10 minutes) for the pilot. This materially reduces short-call billables without changing semantics. We can include an Appendix in the MSA that defines amortization windows and micro‑quantum rules so both teams have a precise reference.

Happy to signal these concessions on the quote if you want formal language.

Markus Klein
Head of Pricing
Redwood Inference
